extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing stand-up comedians, comedy students, and performers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing, timing, and performing stand-up comedy material (one-liners, storytelling, crowd work, and club performance). Emphasis on joke structure, delivery, stagecraft, and audience management.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurry a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating a joke to an audience faster than they can comprehend the Setup's relationship to the Punchline, which can diminish or kill the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: deliver the punchline too quickly without allowing the setup to build properly. Example: 'The comedian hurried the joke, missing the perfect pause before the punchline.' See also rush a joke and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: rush a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating a joke to an audience faster than they can comprehend the Setup's relationship to the Punchline, which diminishes or kills the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same failure mode as 'hurry a joke' — timing needs to let audience process setup before punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurt line
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective psychological tipping point when the pain within the comedy becomes real and turns mood into drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundary criterion: a hurt line is a sharp, cutting remark intended to sting or embarrass. Use with caution — can silence or shock a room. Example: used in response to hecklers; can produce stunned silence before laughter. See dramedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: improvisation / improv
rubrics_metrics.description: The spontaneous creation of bits and sketches not planned beforehand; in comedy, creating material spontaneously with a troupe or via crowd work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill criterion: know fundamental techniques and games of improvising. Related to ad-lib, riff, and crowd work.

rubrics_metrics.name: inside joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor based on common-knowledge information only known by a select institution, group, or people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-limiting criterion: inside jokes will only land with those who share the referenced knowledge. Use sparingly unless the audience is that group.

rubrics_metrics.name: intro / introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prewritten announcement said by an MC, often comical, about comedians, performers, and presenters as they come to the stage or podium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance prep: a good intro often is funny and sets the performer up well; writers/MCs should craft intros that make both MC and guest look good.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke (definition and structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single unit of humor, often two sections: Setup and Punchline, linked by the 5 mechanisms (Connector: 1 thing with 2 interpretations). Setup establishes a Target Assumption; Punchline communicates a Reinterpretation that shatters the Target Assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational rubric: evaluate if setup creates a clear target assumption and connector, and whether punchline delivers an unexpected reinterpretation. See Greg Dean's model and joke structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke structure (Greg Dean / 5 mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model demonstrating two sections (setup and punchline) linked by 5 mechanisms: 1st Story, Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation, and 2nd Story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to diagnose and fix jokes: identify Target Assumption, Connector and Reinterpretation. Evaluate where to place reveal for maximum surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: reveal (reveal placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific information (words, phrases, or actions) that communicate the Reinterpretation, best placed near or at the end of the Punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance guidance: position the reveal at/near punchline to maximize surprise. Misplacing it telegraphs the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Assumption / Connector / Reinterpretation (TCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: TCR: Target Assumption is the expected interpretation of the Connector established by the Setup; Reinterpretation is the unexpected meaning expressed by the Punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical rubric: ensure the connector truly supports two plausible interpretations and that the punchline forces reinterpretation rather than confirming expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: telegraphing
rubrics_metrics.description: Causing the audience to guess the Punchline before it's delivered, usually because the Setup has too much information or acting choices lead the audience prematurely to the Punchline idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: prune setup details and adjust acting to avoid giving away the punchline. See misdirection and joke structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: pause / take a beat / one-liner timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Silence after a punchline to allow time for audience laughter; specifically, one-liner timing: after delivering a punchline, wait for the laugh to peak and then pause for a count (2,3,4) before next setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential timing skill: pausing prevents stepping on laughs. 'Take a beat' and 'pause' improve comedic tempo and allow laughs to peak.

rubrics_metrics.name: step on laughs / talk over laughs / kill a laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes or actions after a punchline that cause audiences to not laugh or stop laughing (continuing to speak, wrong wording, timing errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: avoid continuing dialogue after a punchline; respect laugh cycles. 'Talk over laughs' often kills momentum; practice staying silent in the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: stay in the bit
rubrics_metrics.description: After a Punchline during audience laughter, stop talking and remain in the same emotion/state as when the joke was delivered to give the audience permission and space to laugh and to keep momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance technique coined by Jerry Seinfeld. Helps maintain rhythm and prepares for next joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: timing / comedy timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempo and rhythm developed between comedian and audience while performing; also estimating length of routines/shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core evaluative dimension: assess tempo, rhythm, pauses, and how delivery matches audience response. Practice to calibrate timing to different rooms and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: telegraphing / over-information (as failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing too many clues in the setup or acting so the audience anticipates the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit setups to preserve misdirection; use acting choices to hide the punchline's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: punchline (punch / punch-premise)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second part of jokes meant to get a laugh, expressing the Reinterpretation of the Connector; punch-premise is a statement with a negative opinion constructed as a step in joke mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines should deliver shock/surprise and be concise; punch-premises can be used as writing prompts in joke maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: setup / Setup-Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: First part of jokes designed to misdirect; Setup-Premise is a step requiring a positive-opinion statement to write a series of setups that misdirect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing rubric: craft setups that establish a plausible Target Assumption without revealing the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: rule of three / rhythm of three
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke format where setup lists two positive items, and the punchline reveals a third negative/unexpected item, creating surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural device: useful template for list jokes and punchlines. Evaluate economy and surprise of the third item.

rubrics_metrics.name: tag / tag timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional short punchline immediately following a punchline that doesn't need a new setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tags to extend laughs and increase LPMs; tag timing requires listening for peak laughter and pausing appropriately before adding tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: one-liners / one-liner timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short jokes using a setup and a punchline; timing requires waiting for laugh to peak then pausing for a count before starting next setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery rubric: maintain crispness and proper pause lengths to keep rhythm and avoid stepping on laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: storytelling / storytelling joke structure / scene work
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer narrative jokes told from Narrator POV that include scenes acted out with Self and Character POVs; require acting, staging, tenses, and psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance criterion: evaluate acting choices, POV shifts, scene work, and distribution of setup/punch/tag across POVs. Storytelling requires stronger acting and staging skills than one-liners.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV roles (Narrator POV, Self POV, Character POV, POV shifts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three perceptual positions/comedic roles used in scene work; Narrator talks to audience, Self/Character are used inside scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing/performing rubric: decide which POV delivers which lines; effective POV shifts enhance scenes and jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: read on material
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers judge audience responses (laughter, groans, silence, applause) to know how to adjust their script to get consistent laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-feedback loop: skill in reading the room and adapting material is crucial. Use feedback to punch up/trim or replace bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: tailor (material to audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting or altering material to fit a unique performing situation and different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rubric: adjust references, examples, and emphasis to match audience demographics (e.g., police audience). Helps increase relatability and laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: riff
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique in crowd work where comedians take an idea from an audience response and embellish it to discover humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative skill: measure ability to extend an idea spontaneously, generating new punchlines and tags from audience input.

rubrics_metrics.name: crowd work (implied via riff and improv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working the audience directly, using interactions to generate material on the spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by how well the performer adapts, finds humor, and includes the audience without losing control or stepping on laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: mic technique / microphone / mic stand / mic cord
rubrics_metrics.description: Most effective ways of holding and moving the microphone, stand, and cord to enhance communication and smoothly get performers on and off stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stagecraft criterion: good mic technique avoids distractions, supports vocal clarity and movement, and complements physical comedy if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: smooth on and smooth off
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for getting on stage and off stage to ensure well-run shows (phrase coined by Jerry Seinfeld).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professionalism metric: clean entrances/exits maintain show flow and bookers' goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: respect the light / light / red light / run the light
rubrics_metrics.description: Signals to comedians their performing time is up or nearly up; 'run the light' is continuing after being given the light, which can get a comedian forced off or banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professionalism and timing: adhere to club time signals to avoid conflicts with MCs, other acts, and club management.

rubrics_metrics.name: stage time / time slot / set list / show list
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration and order of jokes/routines allotted to a performer; set/set list helps order material for a show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical planning: build a set appropriate to the time slot; use show lists to remember order and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: laughs per minute (LPMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement for counting the number of laughs in routines or shows (e.g., professional level ~5 LPMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metric: use LPMs to evaluate commercial viability and pacing of material over a set; track changes after edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: opening line
rubrics_metrics.description: First joke of a stand-up show intended to get a laugh in the first fifteen seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical slot: an effective opening line warms the room and starts the LPMs; choose a strong hook to establish tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: material conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: When comedians in the same lineup have similar topics, premises, or jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming/ethical criterion: avoid overlapping material with other performers in the same show; tailor or change topics to prevent conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: punch up / punch down
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch up: make jokes about people/institutions with higher status than the comedian; punch down: targeting those with lower status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/strategic rubric: punching up is often safer and more acceptable; punching down can alienate audience and cross hurt lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurt lines, laser beam topics, and controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics, premises, or jokes that set off public controversy (laser beam) or cross subjective hurt lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessment: evaluate potential fallout and audience consequences; controversial 'laser beam' material can generate attention but may damage career or room rapport.

rubrics_metrics.name: telemetry: public domain / ownership of topics
rubrics_metrics.description: All topics and premises are in the public domain; individual jokes have natural copyright but enforcement is difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative-ownership awareness: don't expect exclusive claims to topics; focus on distinctive angles and style rather than assuming ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: jokey (cliché / hack)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious or cliché jokes; performance that sounds written or forced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality anti-pattern: editing for naturalness and originality reduces 'jokey' feel. Avoid hack material and comic clichés.
